🇵🇸George Town, Grand CaymanTender
Tender ashore · British Caribbean charm
The Cayman Islands' capital is a bright, easygoing Caribbean town of pastel storefronts and impossibly clear water — the calmest, most polished landfall in the western Caribbean, and a fitting first port.
⛵ Booked Shore Excursion
Dolphin Encounter & Stingray Sandbar
Dec 31
ⓘ Good to know
This is a hands-on, in-water outing — a short boat ride to the sandbar, then wading into waist-deep water to meet the stingrays and dolphins. Grand Cayman is a tender port (a short boat shuttles you from ship to shore). Wonderful fun, but more active and wet than a scenic drive — wear what you can get in the water.
📖 Expand — George Town, Grand Cayman
DestinationGrand Cayman is the largest of the three Cayman Islands and one of the Caribbean's safest, most prosperous ports. Beyond the famous Seven Mile Beach, the waters off George Town are a protected marine park — the Stingray Sandbar, where southern stingrays gather in chest-deep water, is the island's signature experience.
Port InfoCayman Islands (British Overseas Territory) · English · Cayman Islands dollar (US dollars accepted everywhere). Tender port — ships anchor in the harbour and shuttle guests to the George Town waterfront by tender boat.
Your ExcursionDolphin Encounter & Stingray Sandbar — a boat transfer to the sandbar followed by in-water interaction with stingrays and a dolphin encounter. Activity level moderate: getting in and out of the boat and standing in moving water. Not a walking tour — the physical ask is the water itself, not distance.

🇨🇴Cartagena, ColombiaDock
Alongside · a walled colonial masterpiece
Cartagena is the jewel of Spain's old Caribbean empire — a UNESCO-listed walled city of balconied mansions, bougainvillea, plazas and fortress ramparts, all in warm colonial stone. The most atmospheric port of the whole voyage, and one made for slow wandering.
⛵ Booked Shore Excursion
Cartagena's Rich Gastronomy
Jan 2
ⓘ Good to know
A culinary tour that suits your taste exactly — arepas, posta cartagenera, coconut sweets, with a photo stop at the San Felipe fortress. The one thing to pace: it winds on foot through the walled Old Town's cobblestone lanes, so wear cushioned shoes and take the shade breaks.
📖 Expand — Cartagena, Colombia
DestinationFounded in 1533, Cartagena de Indias was the fortified treasure-port of the Spanish Main. Its old town — the Ciudad Amurallada — survives almost intact behind eleven kilometres of stone walls, guarded by the great hilltop Castillo San Felipe de Barajas. It is one of the best-preserved colonial cities in the Americas.
Port InfoColombia · Spanish · Colombian peso (US dollars widely accepted at the port). Docks alongside at the Sociedad Portuaria cruise terminal, which has its own small tropical bird garden between ship and gate.
Your ExcursionCartagena's Rich Gastronomy — a tasting walk through the walled Old Town sampling the city's signature dishes, with a photo stop at Castillo San Felipe. Style match is excellent (culinary, unhurried, flavourful). Terrain note: cobblestone streets and periods of standing; rated an active walking tour, so pace it and hydrate.

🇵🇦 The Marquee Day · Panama Canal Transit
7
Mon

4
🇵🇦Panama Canal TransitFull-Day Transit
Atlantic to Pacific · ~50 miles · a full day on deck
This is the heart of the voyage. From the early morning approach off Colón, Seven Seas Grandeur enters the historic locks and is lifted, chamber by chamber, some 85 feet up to Gatún Lake — drawn snug by the little "mule" locomotives that have guided ships since 1914. You glide across the jungle-fringed lake and through the Culebra Cut, the mountain gorge that cost more to carve than any other stretch, then descend the Pacific locks to the sea beyond. Bring coffee to the balcony at dawn; this is a day to simply be on deck and watch a century-old marvel work around you.
📖 Expand — Panama Canal
HistoryOpened in 1914 after a French attempt collapsed and a US effort finally succeeded at the cost of tens of thousands of lives, the Panama Canal remains one of the engineering wonders of the modern world. A ship is raised and lowered a total of about 170 feet across the crossing, using only gravity-fed fresh water from Gatún Lake — no pumps.
What to watchThe line-handling and the electric ‘mule’ locomotives at the Gatún and Miraflores locks; the narrow Culebra (Gaillard) Cut; the Centennial and Bridge of the Americas crossings overhead. Narration is piped across the ship through the day. No excursion — the transit is the experience.

🇨🇷Puntarenas, Costa RicaDock
Alongside · gateway to the cloud forests
Costa Rica's Pacific port opens onto the country's legendary green interior — misty cloud forests, hummingbirds, waterfalls and the pura vida ease that made this the eco-travel capital of the Americas.
⛵ Booked Shore Excursion
A Walk in the Clouds
Jan 5
ⓘ Good to know
Be aware this is the most active outing on the itinerary and the least like your usual scenic/culinary style: a roughly 1¾-hour drive each way to a cloud-forest reserve, then a guided walk over suspension bridges with around 90 steps and up-and-down hill trails. Spectacular for the fit and adventurous — but if a gentler, low-distance option is preferred, Regent offers alternatives at this port worth a look before final excursion booking (due June 2, 2026).
📖 Expand — Puntarenas, Costa Rica
DestinationPuntarenas is the long sandbar port on Costa Rica's central Pacific coast and the jumping-off point for the country's famous cloud forests and national parks. The cloud forest is a rare high-altitude ecosystem — perpetually misty, hung with moss and orchids, alive with hummingbirds and the resplendent quetzal.
Port InfoCosta Rica · Spanish · Costa Rican colón (US dollars accepted). Docks alongside at the Puntarenas cruise pier; the town's Paseo de los Turistas beachfront is walkable from the ship.
Your ExcursionA Walk in the Clouds — a scenic inland drive (~1h45 each way) to a cloud-forest reserve for a naturalist-led walk across suspension bridges, with roughly 90 stairs and up/down trails. Regent activity level is at the higher end. Genuinely beautiful; genuinely a hike. Flagged here honestly given the walking and stairs involved.

🇬🇹Puerto Quetzal, GuatemalaDock
Alongside · gateway to colonial Antigua
Guatemala's Pacific port is the doorway to Antigua — the ravishing former colonial capital cradled by three volcanoes, its cobbled streets lined with pastel churches, ruined convents and the great yellow arch of Santa Catalina.
⛵ Booked Shore Excursion
Casa Santo Domingo (Antigua)
Jan 7
ⓘ Good to know
A lovely cultural-and-culinary day that fits your style well — a restored monastery-hotel with museums, gardens and lunch. Two things to pace: it's a roughly 1¼–1½-hour drive each way (mostly seated) and Antigua's charm comes on cobblestone streets, so easy shoes and an unhurried stroll are the move.
📖 Expand — Puerto Quetzal & Antigua, Guatemala
DestinationAntigua Guatemala, a UNESCO World Heritage site, was the seat of Spanish colonial Central America until earthquakes moved the capital in 1773. What remains is one of the finest colonial townscapes anywhere — baroque facades, jacaranda-shaded plazas, and the iconic Santa Catalina Arch framing the Volcán de Agua.
Port InfoGuatemala · Spanish · Guatemalan quetzal (US dollars accepted on tours). Docks alongside at Puerto Quetzal; a small craft-market and marimba welcome greet the pier. Antigua is roughly 90 km / a scenic 75–90 minute drive inland.
Your ExcursionCasa Santo Domingo — a visit to the restored Santo Domingo monastery, now a five-star hotel and cultural centre with six small museums and gardens, with time in Antigua and lunch. Mostly coach and grounds; the physical ask is the drive time and Antigua's cobbles. Good style fit.

🇲🇽Acapulco, MexicoDock
Alongside · the storied Pacific bay
The original glamour resort of the Mexican Riviera curls around one of the most beautiful bays in the Pacific. Acapulco's mid-century golden age still lingers in its clifftop views — and in the daredevils of La Quebrada, who have been diving its narrow gorge for generations.
⛵ Booked Shore Excursion
Historical, Picturesque & Cliff Divers
Jan 9
ⓘ Good to know
A comfortable, mostly seated bus tour of the bay's landmarks and viewpoints, ending with the famous La Quebrada cliff divers — which you watch as a spectator (the divers do the diving). The name sounds active; your part is gentle. Expect some standing at viewpoints in the sun — a hat and water help.
📖 Expand — Acapulco, Mexico
DestinationAcapulco rose to fame in the 1950s and '60s as the jet-set's Pacific playground, and its horseshoe bay remains a genuine stunner. La Quebrada's cliff divers — who plunge 35 metres into a narrow surging inlet, timing the swell — have performed here since 1934 and are the city's enduring emblem.
Port InfoMexico · Spanish · Mexican peso (US dollars accepted). Docks alongside at the Terminal Marítima pier beside Old Acapulco — no tender.
Your ExcursionHistorical, Picturesque & Cliff Divers — a panoramic city drive taking in the old town, cathedral and bay overlooks, culminating in the La Quebrada cliff-diving show viewed from a terrace. Largely coach-based and spectator; low walking. A good fit, with sun exposure the main thing to manage.

🇲🇽Cabo San Lucas, MexicoTender
Tender ashore · Land's End
Where the Baja peninsula finally runs out of land, the desert meets the sea in a tumble of golden rock — crowned by El Arco, the natural stone arch at Land's End. Sea lions bask on the rocks; the water glows turquoise. The most photogenic anchorage of the voyage.
⛵ Booked Shore Excursion
Arch Exploration & Clear Boat Experience
Jan 11
ⓘ Good to know
Beautifully suited to a scenic, low-effort day — a seated boat cruise (about 45–60 minutes) out to El Arco, Lover's Beach and the sea-lion colony, on a clear-hull boat that lets you see the marine life below. Cabo is a tender port; the only physical step is boarding the tender and the tour boat, so take the crew's hand at the gangway.
📖 Expand — Cabo San Lucas, Mexico
DestinationCabo San Lucas sits at the very southern tip of Baja California, where the Pacific meets the Sea of Cortez. Its signature landmark, El Arco (Land's End), is a wave-cut granite arch surrounded by sea-lion colonies and Lover's/Divorce beaches — best seen, as here, from the water.
Port InfoMexico · Spanish · Mexican peso (US dollars accepted). Tender port — the ship anchors in the bay and tenders guests to the marina, right in the heart of town.
Your ExcursionArch Exploration & Clear Boat Experience — a short, seated clear-hull boat cruise around El Arco, Lover's Beach and the sea-lion rocks, with above- and below-water viewing. Minimal walking; the scenic, leisurely fit is excellent. Tender and boat boarding are the only mobility notes.

🇺🇸San Diego, CaliforniaDock
Alongside · the Embarcadero
San Diego offers the softest of landings back in the States — a sparkling harbour city of near-perfect weather, a historic waterfront, and the barking sea lions of La Jolla just up the coast. An easy, sunlit day before the voyage ends.
⛵ Booked Shore Excursion
San Diego Seal Tour
Jan 13
ⓘ Good to know
One of the best-fitting outings of the trip — the SEAL Tour is a fully seated, narrated amphibious vehicle (“Sea And Land”) that drives the waterfront and then splashes into the bay, with front-row views of the sea lions, the USS Midway and the Star of India. No walking to speak of — just sit back and enjoy.
📖 Expand — San Diego, California
DestinationSan Diego is California's original city and one of America's finest natural harbours, ringed by the Embarcadero, Balboa Park, the Gaslamp Quarter and the seaside village of La Jolla, whose rocks and coves are a haven for barking California sea lions.
Port InfoUnited States · English · US dollar. Docks alongside at the B Street Pier / cruise terminal on the downtown Embarcadero — walkable to Seaport Village and the waterfront.
Your ExcursionSan Diego Seal Tour — a 90-to-100-minute narrated tour aboard a Coast-Guard-approved amphibious vehicle that tours downtown by road, then enters San Diego Bay for sea-lion and harbour viewing. Fully seated, gentle, scenic — the strongest mobility fit of the voyage.

Voyage ends · San Pedro (Port of Los Angeles)
